ordered_diagnoses: metaplastic breast carcinoma with squamous differentiation

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic facial swelling and skin lesions with a history of malignancy
salient_findings: Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face
Pain on palpation without fever or chills
Histopathological findings of atypical cells in dilated vessels
key_facts: 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on the face
History of left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
Treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
Left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision seven years after initial diagnosis
No fever or chills
Pain on palpation
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek
Predominantly involving the left side of the face
Histopathological examination showed hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
Immunohistochemical examination showed epithelial cells in dilated vessels positive for CD31 and atypical cells positive for GATA3

raw.rationale: The patient's history of left breast carcinoma and subsequent metastasis to the left supraclavicular lymph nodes, combined with the current facial symptoms and histopathological findings of atypical cells in dilated vessels, suggests that the facial lesions are metastatic in nature.

rejected.label: metaplastic breast carcinoma with squamous differentiation
rejected.why: There is no indication of squamous differentiation in the provided histopathological examination results.

rejected.label: lymphoma
rejected.why: The immunohistochemical examination results do not support a diagnosis of lymphoma, as the atypical cells were positive for GATA3, which is more commonly associated with breast cancer.

rejected.label: hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of family history make this diagnosis unlikely, and the histopathological findings do not support a diagnosis of hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia.

rejected.label: dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and histopathological findings do not match those typically seen in dermatomyositis, which is characterized by muscle weakness and specific skin changes not described in this case.
